events.title: The Musashi plain
events.body: Forest, marsh and a wide bay. A few fishing and farming villages line the shore

events.title: A statue in the net
events.body: Two fishermen pull a small statue of Kannon from the Sumida River, the legend says

events.title: Sensō-ji
events.body: A temple is built for the statue at Asakusa. It is Tokyo's oldest temple

events.title: The Edo clan
events.body: A warrior family named Edo builds a fortified house on the hill above the bay

events.title: Edo Castle
events.body: The general Ōta Dōkan builds a castle on the hill. A small town grows below it

events.title: Dōkan is killed
events.body: Ōta Dōkan is murdered by his own lord. The castle passes from hand to hand

events.title: The Hōjō take Edo
events.body: The Hōjō clan's army captures the castle and holds it for 66 years

events.title: Tokugawa Ieyasu arrives
events.body: Given the eastern provinces, Ieyasu marches in with his army and makes Edo his base

events.title: Making land from the sea
events.body: The Hibiya inlet is filled in with earth from the Kanda hill. Edo grows into the bay

events.title: The shogun's capital
events.body: Ieyasu becomes shogun. Nihonbashi bridge is built; Japan's main roads start here

events.title: A five-storey keep
events.body: The tallest castle keep in Japan rises over Edo

events.title: Daimyo processions
events.body: Every lord must spend alternate years in Edo. Their armies march in long processions

events.title: The Great Meireki Fire
events.body: Fire burns for three days. Most of Edo and the castle keep are lost. Over 100,000 die

events.title: Rebuilt wider
events.body: Firebreaks and wider streets are laid out. The keep is never rebuilt

events.title: Ryōgoku bridge
events.body: A bridge across the Sumida opens new land to the east

events.title: A city of a million
events.body: Edo is now one of the largest cities in the world

events.title: Fireworks on the Sumida
events.body: The Ryōgoku fireworks begin, a summer tradition that still continues

events.title: The Great Meiwa Fire
events.body: Another great fire sweeps across the city

events.title: The Black Ships
events.body: US Commodore Perry's warships sail into Edo Bay and demand that Japan open its ports

events.title: The Ansei earthquake
events.body: A powerful earthquake strikes Edo. Fires break out across the lowlands

events.title: The Sakuradamon Incident
events.body: In the snow, samurai kill the shogun's chief minister outside the castle gate

events.title: A city surrendered
events.body: The shogun's men hand over Edo Castle to the imperial army without a fight

events.title: The Battle of Ueno
events.body: Imperial troops storm the hill where the last Shōgitai samurai hold out. The temple burns

events.title: Tokyo is born
events.body: Edo is renamed Tokyo, 'Eastern Capital'. The young Emperor Meiji arrives in a grand procession

events.title: The first railway
events.body: Japan's first railway opens from Shimbashi. Ginza is rebuilt in brick

events.title: A modern capital
events.body: Brick offices, gas lamps, rickshaws and trams fill the streets

events.title: Tokyo Station
events.body: A grand red-brick station opens in front of the Imperial Palace

events.title: Meiji Shrine
events.body: A shrine is built in a new forest planted with 100,000 trees donated from across Japan

events.title: The Great Kantō earthquake
events.body: At noon the earth shakes. Fires burn for two days. More than 100,000 people die

events.title: Ruins
events.body: Nearly half of Tokyo is destroyed

events.title: Rebuilding
events.body: New avenues, steel bridges and concrete schools rise from the ruins

events.title: The February 26 Incident
events.body: Young army officers lead 1,400 soldiers to seize the centre of Tokyo. The revolt fails

events.title: The firebombing of Tokyo
events.body: At night US bombers drop firebombs on the eastern districts. About 100,000 die

events.title: The city burns again
events.body: More raids leave half of Tokyo in ruins

events.title: Surrender
events.body: The war ends. Allied forces occupy Japan until 1952

events.title: Tokyo Tower
events.body: At 333 m, a red and white tower rises over the rebuilt city

events.title: The Olympic Games
events.body: Asia's first Olympics. The bullet train opens days before

events.title: Sunshine 60
events.body: Skyscrapers begin to rise in Ikebukuro, Shinjuku and beyond

events.title: The bubble years
events.body: Tokyo's land is said to be worth more than all of California

events.title: A new city hall
events.body: The twin-towered Metropolitan Government Building opens in Shinjuku

events.title: Rainbow Bridge
events.body: A suspension bridge links the city to the new waterfront at Odaiba

events.title: The Great East Japan Earthquake
events.body: Buildings sway across Tokyo. The city's earthquake-proof towers stand

events.title: Tokyo Skytree
events.body: At 634 m, the tallest tower in the world opens beside the Sumida

events.title: The Olympics return
events.body: Delayed a year by the pandemic, the Games are held without spectators

events.title: Tokyo today
events.body: About 14 million people live in Tokyo, and 37 million in the region
